name: MonkeyOCRv2-Parsing (S 0.6B, B 0.7B)
vendor: HUST (Xiang Bai, Yuliang Liu groups; HF org zenosai)

lineage.how_derived: frozen document-native ViT encoder (MonkeyOCRv2-S 28M / -B 113M) paired with a small language model; earlier generation MonkeyOCR-pro (1.2B/3B, 2025)

purpose: Multilingual document parsing (17 languages, digital and photographed pages) from a vision encoder pretrained on documents instead of natural images, which the authors argue is needed for dense text and fine character strokes (arXiv 2607.11562 abstract).

license.name: Apache-2.0 (code and all weights); MonkeyDoc v2 annotations CC BY 4.0
license.notes: GitHub LICENSE file read: "The code and all MonkeyOCRv2 model weights (encoders, Parsing, Und) are released under the Apache License 2.0 ... MonkeyDoc v2 annotations are released under CC BY 4.0; see the dataset card for image-source terms." The file is this short grant, not the full Apache text (GitHub reports license metadata NOASSERTION); the HF card tag and card text agree ("free for both research and commercial use"). The HF repos carry no LICENSE file.

architecture.kind: vision-language: ViT-B (12 layers, 113M) + Qwen3-shaped decoder (28 layers, hidden 1024, 16 heads / 8 KV heads, per config.json), custom code (monkeyocrv2)
architecture.why_this_design: general visual encoders are pretrained on natural images; the encoder here is pretrained with image-to-text generation plus pixel-level document reconstruction on 113M document images (MonkeyDoc v2), then frozen under a lightweight LLM (arXiv abstract). The decoder family is inferred from config.json, the card does not name it.

variants.notes: 0.88B parameters per HF API incl. vision; 152,298 downloads; created 2026-07-11
speculative drafter for vLLM, card says up to 2x faster inference

pc-16gb.notes: under 2 GB of BF16 weights; Tona runs one model at a time, so it replaces the resident model while it works

engine_support.notes: no GGUF found in an HF search for MonkeyOCR on 2026-11-19 for v2 (only community GGUFs of the 2025 MonkeyOCR); custom architecture needs a llama.cpp port

benchmarks.name: MDPBench German pages (DE column)
benchmarks.harness: official MDPBench leaderboard; the benchmark authors list it, the vendor reports the same row on its card

strengths: best German and overall MDPBench score among all specialised open parsers listed (DE 87.7 vs Chandra 86.6, PaddleOCR-VL-1.5 84.8, GLM-OCR 82.7)
integrated by RAGFlow as a PDF parser (card news 2026-09-07)
weaknesses: very new (July 2026), no community user reports beyond the vendor news and the RAGFlow integration
custom-code architecture, no GGUF or llama.cpp port
its main benchmark is the vendor-adjacent MDPBench; no OmniDocBench or olmOCR-bench numbers read for it
training corpus partly synthetic (52M synthetic + 52M real samples released)
best_for: German and multilingual scans and photographed pages parsed to text/markdown
soft.maturity: GitHub repo created 2026-07-10, 1669 stars and 0 open issues at check time; ongoing releases (CPU support, DFlash drafter, training code)

user_reports.summary: RAGFlow announced MonkeyOCRv2-Parsing as a supported PDF parser (vendor card news, not an independent report)

tona_fit.reason: highest third-party German score of all parsers checked, 0.7B, Apache-2.0 verified, fits every hardware class; it is the first model to test against PaddleOCR-VL and GLM-OCR on our German scans. Missing Tona and llama.cpp support are blockers only.
blockers: Tona engine has no vision/OCR architecture
no GGUF / llama.cpp port for the monkeyocrv2 architecture
